name: Imbalanced Arrays
description: Ntarsis has come up with an array $$$a$$$ of $$$n$$$ non-negative integers. Call an array $$$b$$$ of $$$n$$$ integers imbalanced if it satisfies the following: $$$-n\le b_i\le n$$$, $$$b_i \ne 0$$$, there are no two indices $$$(i, j)$$$ ($$$1 \le i, j \le n$$$) such that $$$b_i + b_j = 0$$$, for each $$$1 \leq i \leq n$$$, there are exactly $$$a_i$$$ indices $$$j$$$ ($$$1 \le j \le n$$$) such that $$$b_i+b_j \gt 0$$$, where $$$i$$$ and $$$j$$$ are not necessarily distinct. Given the array $$$a$$$, Ntarsis wants you to construct some imbalanced array. Help him solve this task, or determine it is impossible.
input_specification: Each test contains multiple test cases. The first line contains the number of test cases $$$t$$$ ($$$1 \le t \le 10^5$$$). The description of the test cases follows. The first line of each test case has a single integer $$$n$$$ ($$$1 \leq n \leq 10^5$$$). The next line contains $$$n$$$ integers $$$a_1, a_2, \ldots, a_n$$$ ($$$0 \leq a_i \leq n$$$). It is guaranteed that the sum of $$$n$$$ across all test cases does not exceed $$$10^5$$$.
output_specification: For each test case, output " NO " if there exists no imbalanced array. Otherwise, output " YES ". Then, on the next line, output $$$n$$$ integers $$$b_1, b_2, \ldots, b_n$$$ where $$$b_i \neq 0$$$ for all $$$1 \leq i \leq n$$$ — an imbalanced array.
approach_summary: Exploit monotonicity of two-pointer invariant [L, R]. Advance R while shifting L forward to maintain validity, running in O(N) amortized time.

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 1852B — Imbalanced Arrays [34. Two Pointers]
topic_editorial.key_invariant: When scanning contiguous subarrays or paired indices, advancing the right pointer $R$ monotonically tightens or relaxes the constraint, allowing the left pointer $L$ to only advance forward without ever needing to reset backwards.
